name: London
title: Holidays in London
intro: Royal palaces, free world-class museums, West End shows and a different neighbourhood around every corner. Here's what London is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Tower Bridge over the River Thames in London on a bright day

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No passport checks within the UK

facts_note: UK and Irish citizens don't need a passport to travel within the UK, but airlines ask for photo ID. Most other visitors need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA), so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are the best months, with long, mild days and parks at their best. July and August are the warmest and busiest, with school holiday crowds at the big sights. December is cold but festive, with Christmas lights, markets and ice rinks. January and February are grey but hotels are cheaper. Rain can come at any time of year, so pack a jacket.

things.name: British Museum
things.blurb: Egyptian mummies, the Rosetta Stone and two million years of history, all free to visit.

things.name: Tower of London
things.blurb: Nearly a thousand years of history, the Crown Jewels and the Beefeaters, right beside Tower Bridge.

things.name: South Bank walk
things.blurb: Stroll the Thames from the London Eye past Shakespeare's Globe and Tate Modern to Borough Market.

things.name: Natural History Museum
things.blurb: Dinosaurs, a blue whale skeleton and the earthquake room, with the Science Museum next door.

things.name: A West End show
things.blurb: Musicals and plays in the theatres around Leicester Square and Covent Garden.

things.name: Greenwich
things.blurb: Take the boat down the Thames to the Cutty Sark, the Royal Observatory and the Prime Meridian.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in London?
faqs.answer: Three or four days covers the big sights at a gentle pace. A week lets you add Greenwich, Kew Gardens or a day trip to Windsor, Oxford or Cambridge.

faqs.question: Are London's museums free?
faqs.answer: Yes. The British Museum, Natural History Museum, Science Museum, National Gallery, Tate Modern and V&A are all free, though some special exhibitions charge.

faqs.question: What is the best way to get around London?
faqs.answer: The Underground and buses. Tap in with a contactless card or phone, and daily fares are capped. Under-11s travel free with an adult.

faqs.question: Which London airport is best?
faqs.answer: Heathrow has the most long-haul flights and the Elizabeth line into central London. Gatwick, Stansted, Luton and London City are also well linked by train.
